channel.title: Updated · Biology
channel.description: Life sciences: discoveries, medicine and biotech

item.title: Health Canada warns of a very rare risk of sudden vision loss with semaglutide drugs
item.description: Health Canada's completed safety review found a possible link between prescription semaglutide and NAION, a form of sudden, usually permanent vision loss, and product labels will be updated. (Health Canada, CBC News via Radio Canada International, Global News)

item.title: Flu admissions in England jump almost 80% in a week, the highest for late November since before Covid
item.description: Hospital admissions for flu in England rose from five to nearly nine per 100,000 people in a week, the highest for this point in November this decade, with vaccination lagging. (BBC News, The Guardian)

item.title: An engineered cohesion system reduces errors in aged mammalian eggs
item.description: An engineered protein glue called TALhesin held chromosome halves together in aged mouse eggs, raising the share of error-free eggs from 46.7% to 74.1%, close to the level in young mice. (Alexandre Webster, Halima Yusuf, Nina Schweizer et al. · Max Planck Institute for Multidisciplinary Sciences, Göttingen; eggs donated via Göttingen Fertility Center, Bourn Hall Fertility Clinic (Cambridgeshire) and Fertility Center Berlin)

item.title: Licensing mechanisms during RNA-guided DNA integration by type I-F3 CAST
item.description: Structures of a CRISPR-associated transposase revealed how it locks onto a precise genomic target, and redesigned proteins made it 100 times more active without losing on-target specificity. (Shirin Fatma, Shubham Dubey, Vinh H. Truong et al. · St. Jude Children's Research Hospital, Department of Structural Biology)

item.title: In vivo genome-editing therapy for Duchenne muscular dystrophy: Preclinical studies and first-in-human trial
item.description: A single-dose CRISPR therapy delivered by one AAV9 vector produced the first molecular evidence of gene editing in the muscles of boys with Duchenne muscular dystrophy, but one of four participants died. (Guoling Li, Feng Han, Cuijin Wang et al. · HuidaGene Therapeutics (Shanghai), Chinese Academy of Sciences, Shanghai Jiao Tong University)

item.title: The first generic version of the twice-yearly HIV prevention shot lenacapavir arrives in Zambia, at about $40 a year
item.description: The Global Fund says the first generic lenacapavir, a twice-yearly HIV prevention injection expected to cost about $40 per person a year, has reached Zambia, with Uganda next. (The Global Fund, BBC, Associated Press (via Yahoo News))

item.title: Congo's Ebola outbreak passes 12,000 confirmed cases, with only 15% of new cases among known contacts
item.description: Government data show more than 12,000 confirmed Ebola cases in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, and most new cases are still appearing outside known chains of transmission. (US CDC, ECDC, Reuters (via Head Topics))

item.title: Hepatitis B vaccination at birth falls to 65.6% of US newborns, and slips among babies of infected mothers, a records study finds
item.description: An analysis of health records for 1.3 million US infants finds hepatitis B vaccination within a day of birth fell from about 80% in 2022 to 65.6% by June 2026. (Truveta, NEJM Evidence)

item.title: Blood-Pressure–Lowering Treatment across the Cardiovascular Risk Spectrum
item.description: Pooling 51 randomized trials and 357,440 people, blood-pressure drugs cut major cardiovascular events by the same relative amount at every level of predicted risk, but the absolute gain shrinks as risk falls. (Zeinab Bidel Milad Nazarzadeh Borislava Mihaylova Qianqian Yang Johan Sundström Nathalie Conrad Dexter Canoy Guyu Zeng David M. Kent William C. Cushman John Chalmers Koon K. Teo Carl J. Pepine Barry R. Davis Mark Woodward and Kazem Rahimithe Blood Pressure Lowering Treatment Trialists’ Collaboration*)

item.title: Later-born generations have better memory and lose it more slowly
item.description: Across about 219,000 people in five long-running studies, later-born generations enter old age with better memory and lose it more slowly. (Anders Fjell et al. · University of Oslo)

item.title: Middle–Late Pleistocene Denisovans and unresolved Homo in southern China
item.description: Enamel proteins from four teeth found in two caves in Guangxi point to two kinds of archaic human in southern China: one Denisovan-like, one that fits no sampled group. (Song Xing, Huiyun Rao, Guangmao Xie et al. · Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology, Beijing)

item.title: FDA approves bezuclastinib with sunitinib for gastrointestinal stromal tumours after imatinib
item.description: The FDA approved Cogent's Ekitna (bezuclastinib) with sunitinib for advanced gastrointestinal stromal tumours after imatinib; in a phase 3 trial the pair held the cancer in check for a median 16.5 months versus 9.2. (Cogent Biosciences (GlobeNewswire release, via WBOC), Pharmaceutical Technology)

item.title: England records 5,258 heat-associated deaths in 2026, the most since monitoring began
item.description: The UK Health Security Agency estimates 5,258 deaths in England were associated with heat between May and September 2026, far above the previous record of 2,985 in 2022. (The Guardian, BBC)

item.title: Dolphins with larger, more predictable social groups live longer, a 40-year study in Shark Bay finds
item.description: Four decades of observations of about 400 wild bottlenose dolphins show that animals that are more sociable and more consistent in the group sizes they keep tend to live longer. (PLOS Biology, University of Queensland, The Guardian)

item.title: Intensive Blood-Pressure Lowering in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes
item.description: In 9,476 Brazilians with type 2 diabetes, aiming for systolic blood pressure below 120 instead of below 140 mm Hg did not significantly cut cardiovascular events, and kidney-function declines were more frequent. (Karla Santo Eduardo Martins Gisele S. Silva Patricia O. Guimarães Caio A.M. Tavares João B. Andrade Frederico Monfardini Josué Nieri Silvia R.L. Assis João S. Felício Fábio S. Silveira Marcos S. item.title: A shared meaning component across languages in the human brain
item.description: Models trained to predict brain responses to one language also predict responses to languages they never saw, across speakers of 21 languages, pointing to a shared representation of meaning. (Andrea Gregor de Varda, Saima Malik-Moraleda, Greta Tuckute et al. · McGovern Institute for Brain Research and Department of Brain and Cognitive Sciences, MIT)

item.title: Architecture of the poxvirus early-transcription machinery and portal complex
item.description: Imaging of intact vaccinia virus cores shows the virus's gene-copying enzymes parked in pairs beside the genome, next to a channel through the core wall suited to exporting RNA. (Benoît Arragain, Lukas W. Bauer, Victor-Valentin Hodirnau et al. · Institute of Science and Technology Austria (ISTA))

item.title: FDA approves giredestrant after surgery, the first new hormone therapy for early-stage breast cancer in over 20 years
item.description: The FDA approved Roche's daily pill Wilserdly for early breast cancer after surgery, on the strength of a 4,170-patient trial in which it cut recurrence or death by 30% against standard hormone therapy. (FDA, Fierce Pharma)

item.title: FDA approves ribitol, the first treatment for any form of limb-girdle muscular dystrophy
item.description: The FDA approved Welgemda, a twice-daily oral solution, for limb-girdle muscular dystrophy type 2I/R9 after a 112-patient placebo-controlled trial showed gains in walking speed and lung function at 12 months. (FDA, STAT)

item.title: Kymera's once-daily eczema pill cuts disease severity by 72% in a 244-patient mid-stage trial, the company reports
item.description: In a randomized phase 2b trial, an oral drug that destroys the immune signalling protein STAT6 reduced eczema severity scores by 72% against 27% on placebo; the results are company-reported, not yet peer-reviewed. (Kymera Therapeutics press release (via BioSpace), New Scientist, Dermatology Times)

item.title: CMR to Guide Defibrillator Implantation for LVEF
item.description: In a randomized trial of 353 patients with moderately reduced heart function and scarring on cardiac MRI, implanted defibrillators did not significantly reduce sudden cardiac death or serious arrhythmia over 6.3 years. (Joseph B. Selvanayagam, et al. (CMR GUIDE Investigators) · Flinders University and Flinders Medical Centre, Adelaide)

item.title: A glucose-powered artificial neuroimmune axis for metabolic control
item.description: An implant that runs on the body's own glucose stimulated the vagus nerve whenever its fuel-cell voltage signalled high blood sugar, and lowered blood glucose in diabetic rats over weeks. (Weijun Xiu, Qian Wang, Ling Wan et al. · National University of Singapore)

item.title: FDA rejects Capricor's Duchenne cell therapy a second time, citing unreliable data from its phase 3 trial
item.description: The FDA declined again to approve deramiocel for Duchenne muscular dystrophy, saying the phase 3 HOPE-3 trial missed its prespecified goals and that inspection findings made its data unreliable. (Pharmacally, NeurologyLive, Capricor (July 2025 release, background))

item.title: Virginia reports its first measles death of 2026, a young child, as confirmed US cases reach 5,838
item.description: Virginia health officials reported the death of a child aged four or younger who had measles, the 12th such death reported by US states this year, as the CDC's national count reached 5,838 cases. (Virginia Department of Health, CDC, ABC News, The Guardian)

item.title: Merck's antibody-drug conjugate sac-TMT extends survival in heavily pretreated stomach and oesophageal cancer, the company says
item.description: Merck says its 473-patient phase 3 TroFuse-015 trial of sacituzumab tirumotecan met its overall survival goal in third-line gastroesophageal adenocarcinoma, but missed on progression-free survival and released no numbers. (BioPharm International, OncoDaily, The Pharma Letter, Merck)

item.title: Assessing Multiple Treatment Regimens for Tuberculosis
item.description: A platform trial in 401 adults with tuberculosis screened ten new four-drug combinations at once and selected two 16-week regimens, each built around a new drug, for further testing. (Hanif Esmail Nicholas I. Paton Jodie A. Schildkraut Ilaria Motta Alexander J. Szubert Suzanne M. Dufault Norbert Heinrich Simon Tiberi Cissy M. Kityo Timothy D. McHugh Fairoez Ryklief Daniela M. Sloan David Barros-Aguirre and Michael Hoelscherthe PARADIGM4TB (UNITE4TB-01) Trial Team* · University College London; Radboud University Medical Center; National University of Singapore; LMU University Hospital Munich; GSK)

item.title: Multiscale spatial atlas of human basal ganglia cell types and communities
item.description: A spatial map of about 7.9 million cells in four human brains resolves 60 cell types in the basal ganglia and shows how they are arranged, part of a 26-study atlas of the region. (Bereket Tesfay Berackey, Zhiqun Tan, Ginny Wu et al. · University of California, Irvine)

item.title: Divergent activation of the RXFP1 relaxin receptor by protein and small-molecule agonists
item.description: Three cryo-electron microscopy structures show that the hormone relaxin-2 and a small-molecule drug candidate, AZD5462, switch on the same receptor by binding different parts of it and reshaping it differently. (James Osei-Owusu, Tristan Girbau, Xunan Wang et al. · Harvard Medical School)

item.title: A blood protein flags advanced CTE in former football players, a small JAMA study finds
item.description: In 21 former football players who later donated their brains, blood levels of a tau protein fragment were far higher in those with advanced CTE, a preliminary step toward diagnosing the disease in life. (The Boston Globe, AZFamily)

item.title: FDA approves Regeneron's Livsayis, the first gene-silencing drug for generalized myasthenia gravis
item.description: The FDA approved cemdisiran (Livsayis), an injection given four times a year that silences production of the immune protein C5, for adults with antibody-positive generalized myasthenia gravis. (Medical Daily, WebMD, BioPharm International)

item.title: A neural code for generative speech production in human Wernicke’s area
item.description: Recordings from 28 surgical patients show a small spot in Wernicke's area, long seen as a listening region, activates about a quarter-second before each spoken word and is needed for speaking. (Alexander B. Silva, Matthew K. Leonard, Patrick W. Hullett et al. · University of California, San Francisco)

item.title: Evidence for late Middle Pleistocene Homo erectus in mainland East Asia
item.description: Teeth from two caves in Guangxi, dated to between about 324,000 and 184,000 years ago, show Homo erectus survived in southern China's rainforests much later than its previously known disappearance from mainland Asia. (Wei Liao, Clément Zanolli, Ragnheiður Diljá Ásmundsdóttir et al.)

item.title: A daily KRAS-blocking pill plus chemotherapy stops tumour growth in 90% of patients with advanced pancreatic cancer in an early trial
item.description: In a 61-patient phase 1/2 trial, daraxonrasib plus standard chemotherapy shrank tumours in just over 60% of people newly diagnosed with metastatic pancreatic cancer; 76.6% were alive at one year. (BBC News, The Guardian)

item.title: FDA grants accelerated approval to GSK's Nelkarmi for ALK-positive lung cancer that has outgrown earlier drugs
item.description: The FDA cleared neladalkib, a daily pill, for advanced ALK-positive non-small cell lung cancer after earlier ALK inhibitors stop working, based on response rates of 49% and 32% in a 222-patient trial. (pharmaphorum, chemXplore)

item.title: Retatrutide Once Weekly in Adults with Knee Osteoarthritis Pain and Obesity
item.description: In two phase 3 trials with 1,019 adults with obesity and painful knee osteoarthritis, weekly retatrutide injections cut pain scores and body weight significantly more than placebo, with more serious side effects. (Thomas J. Schnitzer David J. Hunter Philip G. Conaghan Arya M. Sharma Sue D. Pedersen Kaiyi Chen So Young Park Nune Makarova Kathryn Giblin and Tammy Forresterthe TRIUMPH-4 and TRIUMPH-1-OA Investigators* · Northwestern University Feinberg School of Medicine; University of Sydney; University of Leeds; University of Alberta; University of Calgary; Eli Lilly and Company)

item.title: A DNA Typewriter records the cell lineage history of a mouse, from zygote to late organogenesis
item.description: A DNA recorder inserted into a fertilized mouse egg wrote an ordered log of cell divisions into the genome, letting researchers rebuild a mouse embryo's cell family tree from the first division to organ formation. (Qi Yu, Haedong Kim, Sophie Seidel et al. · University of Washington School of Medicine; Howard Hughes Medical Institute; Dartmouth College)

item.title: Spatial transcriptomics reveals molecular organization of human and nonhuman primate basal ganglia
item.description: Mapping where each cell type sits in the basal ganglia of humans, macaques and marmosets, researchers found a highly stereotyped layout shared across primates and often with mice, with gene gradients laid over discrete compartments. (Madeleine N. Hewitt, Meghan A. Turner, Nelson Johansen et al. · Allen Institute for Brain Science; Princeton Neuroscience Institute; Leiden University Medical Center; Delft University of Technology; The Rockefeller University; Massachusetts Institute of Technology; Washington University in St. Louis; RIKEN; Kyoto University; University of Washington)

item.title: FDA approves venglustat, the first treatment for the neurological symptoms of type 3 Gaucher disease
item.description: The FDA approved Sanofi's Infilbray (venglustat), a daily pill that reaches the brain, after a 43-patient randomized trial showed better neurological scores than standard enzyme infusions at one year. (FDA)

item.title: An off-the-shelf leukemia vaccine extends survival by nine months in a phase 3 trial, its developers report
item.description: In the 126-patient REGAL trial, people with acute myeloid leukemia in second remission who got the WT1 peptide vaccine galinpepimut-S lived a median 24.0 months, against 14.7 months on other treatments. (Memorial Sloan Kettering, BioPharm International)

item.title: Biogen's tau-lowering drug diranersen shows larger effects at two years in early Alzheimer's, in an open-label extension
item.description: Biogen says the twice-yearly 60 mg dose of diranersen slowed decline on the CDR-SB dementia scale by 38% at two years, up from 26% at 18 months, though the comparison comes from an open-label extension. (Biogen (GlobeNewswire), ReachMD)
